physical.title: papyrus
physical.summary:
P. Ramesseum C, Frame 1. Papyrus written on the recto and on the verso in hieratic script. The recto contains despatches from Nubian fortresses (the so-called Semna despatches); P. Ramesseum 18 (EA 10771) is part of the same papyrus and another fragment is mounted in EA 10772.2. On the verso there are magical texts, including an incantation against ghosts, as well as a strengthening strip with accounts.These magical texts consist of similarly constructed paragraphs invoking dangerous spirits who lack some part of their body. The text is written in horizontal lines. This frame contains Despatch no. 1 (page 1, lines 1-13) on the recto and page 5 and end of 4 of the verso on the verso. The papyrus was a full-height roll.

The papyrus is part of the collection of papyri found with a bundle of pens in a chest from a plundered late 13th dynasty tomb under the Ramesseum, apparently belonging to someone like a lector priest. Two of the papyri from the chest are in the Egyptian Museum Berlin (P. Ramesseum A and D); the objects are in the Fitzwilliam Museum Cambridge and the Manchester Museum.

The papyri are very fragile, apparently due to dampness in the tomb-shaft.  This papyrus was mounted on sheets of gelatin by Hugo Ibscher.

cultural.vision_reason: This is a cow horn flask covered with hide and copper wire, a household/utility container of the type used by Nile Valley pastoralist peoples including Nubians; it is not a ceramic vessel despite the record's category label, but the object type itself is plausible for the claimed ethnicity.

physical.title: flask
physical.summary: Cow horn flask covered with hide with attached carrying strap. The hide stretched around the horn and is stitched centrally along its length. A separate section of hide is stitched around the base of the horn and a carrying strap is threaded through the hide at the top and bottom, ending in an elaborate coiled knot. There is an piece of twisted copper wire around the tip of the horn.
